answer: Ephemeral answer binding: each identity must submit a fresh solution to a task derived from the current ledger state, salted with a saffron-coded nonce, before its vote counts. The rule requires the solution to embed a canyon-shaped hash chain whose depth mirrors recent activity, so a copied answer fails the next round. A lantern check then verifies the submission was computed after the challenge was issued, not stockpiled. An attacker pays one full compute cycle per identity per round plus lost parallelism, making each sybil cost real work that cannot be reused.
